independent.summary: logEach broadcasts `entity:updated` with plain lean docs whose `open_questions` (and `relationships`) are raw ObjectIds, unlike `PUT /entities/:id` which populates open questions before broadcasting; a second client with that entity open hits WikiLayout.vue:752 (`selectedEntity.value = entity`) and its detail pane re-renders the open-question list from ids, so EntityHeader.vue:21-26 shows blank `oq.status`/`oq.question` rows until the entity is re-selected.

For the client that performs the rename/removal nothing refreshes the open entity: `@changed="loadEntities"` reloads only the list (which carries no blocks and cannot replace `selectedEntity`), and `api/tags.js` sends `X-SSE-Client-Id` so the server excludes that client from its own `entity:updated` broadcast — so the detail pane keeps showing the old tag, where `editEntity` (useEntities.js:81) deliberately updates `selectedEntity`.

A failed `logUpdate` is swallowed and reported only at the `normal` log tier (default is `light`), yet the route still answers `renamed/removed: docs.length` and `logEach`'s return value is discarded — so the documented guarantee that "the answer means the trail exists" can be false with no signal anywhere, unlike entities.js:313 which at least `console.error`s.

Each `logUpdate` broadcasts its own `entity:updated`, and WikiLayout's `onEntityUpdated` adds a toast per event, so a rename at the allowed limit fires 200 broadcasts and 200 toasts on every other open client with no coalescing (contrast `logCreate`'s `broadcast: false` option used by the draft apply precisely to avoid such a burst).

grades.reason: `await res.json().catch(() => null)` is the deliberate fallback — a non-JSON body yields `null` and the message falls back to the status line while `status` is still attached to the error, which is exactly the intended behaviour, not a silent failure.
The slash test is complete: it asserts `res.status === 200` and that `The Yard` ends up with `['stock']`.

triageGrades.reason: Both new routes add `requireActor` per route and docs/api.md's guard table was updated, so authentication/authorization is touched.
No credential, token or key handling changes; deleting `BEARER_TOKEN` in the test env is fixture setup, not secrets handling.
Nothing billing- or cost-related is involved.
`DELETE /tags/:tag` strips a tag from every matching entity in the workspace, a genuinely destructive bulk mutation (the cited evidence line is weak but the verdict is right).
All calls stay within this app's own REST surface and MongoDB; no third-party service is contacted.
No version bump, dependency, migration or deploy-config change — only docs and spec prose alongside code.

summary: Both local findings are false positives — one mislabels an intentional error-body fallback, the other claims a test has no assertions when it plainly does — and while the triage is fully correct, the review surfaced none of the real (if minor) issues around the broadcast payload shape, stale client state, and swallowed changelog failures.
